text: A REST API lets applications communicate over the internet. Good API design starts with clear endpoints, such as /users or /orders, that describe the resources they represent. Always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so clients understand what happened. Clear documentation helps developers use your API without confusion. It should explain each endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Versioning is also important. When you change your API, use a version number, for example /v2/users, so old applications keep working. Following these practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
